headline: Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang puts the chance of AI wiping out humanity at zero, while an Anthropic safety researcher puts it above 10% within a decade.
score_reason: A commentary piece that stitches together statements from several weeks; no new event, and some claims are the outlet's own framing. Lowered from 6.
importance_line: It helps readers see the split between AI optimists and safety researchers, but the numbers on both sides are personal judgments, not measurements.
summary: BigGo Finance reports in an analysis that Jensen Huang, chief executive of Nvidia, dismissed AI extinction warnings as a "doomsday narrative" on CBS and named Nobel laureate Geoffrey Hinton on a New York Times podcast, days after Evan Hubinger, an Anthropic alignment researcher, wrote on X that he sees a better than 10% chance of AI-caused human extinction within a decade. Huang's remarks read as a reply to Hubinger's post and to Hinton's long-running warnings; BigGo notes both figures are subjective beliefs, not experimental results.
notes: Full text read. It is an opinion-style analysis; it also retells a July OpenAI-Hugging Face incident (about 1,200 agents) and cites the BBC; those details were not independently checked. Reply link: BigGo ties Huang's CBS/NYT remarks to Hubinger and Hinton; we say 'read as'. Score lowered 6 to 5.
